title: Why Have Indians Become a Regular Target of Hate in Singapore?
author: Asif Ullah Khan
text:
Shops on Serangoon Road in Singapore’s Little India quarter, Apr. 3, 2016.
Credit: Wikimedia Commons/Maksym Kozlenko
When Lee Kuan Yew took Singapore out of the Malaysian Federation on August 9, 1965, he made English the new nation’s primary language of government and education, rather than Chinese, despite the fact that 75 percent of the population was ethnic Chinese. Ensuring that other ethnic minorities did not feel alienated, he also gave Malay, Mandarin, and Tamil official status.After the race riots in 1964 that left 36 people dead, Lee dismantled the city’s deeply segregated colonial setup, where different ethnic groups lived in isolated enclaves, and introduced the Ethnic Integration Policy. This ensured that every building must have a mix of Chinese, Malay, and Indian residents that matches the country’s actual population.[...]
